title: Derive graph-independent planning content identities
description: OBJECTIVE: break the target-graph digest cycle discovered while designing recursive nodeAuthorityHash. CURRENT GAP: PlanRevision.planHash and AcceptanceContract.criteriaDigest both include target graphContentHash, so neither can be embedded in a nodeAuthorityHash that the same graphContentHash covers. DELIVERABLE: focused production derivations over the already-admitted canonical records: one plan execution-content digest over ordered steps/affected node+criterion sets/verification recipes, and per-criterion content digests over node kind plus the actual obligation/evidence/recipe content. These identities exclude only target-graph binding, approval/lifecycle, authorship/lineage/revision IDs and unrelated applicability nodes, use distinct versioned digest domains, return frozen bounded results, and preserve exact upstream refusal code+layer. Do not change either record schema or existing full digest. CONSUMERS: publication task task-dc21cb4a8f2a4c1c902f3bf3a82a59c2 must export the new derivations; the canonical NodeAuthority producer filed after this task will call them.
definitionOfDone: PlanRevision production code derives a domain-separated execution-content digest from version, ordered typed steps, affected node/criterion sets, and verification recipe refs while proving graph binding, approval state, author/lineage/revision ids, rejection state, and planHash do not enter this identity.

AcceptanceContract production code derives a sorted frozen nonempty criterion-id/content-digest roster from version, node kind, statement, evidence requirements, and verification recipe refs; graph/revision/node applicability, author, contract id, and criteriaDigest do not make unrelated criterion content change.

Both APIs first admit through the existing production contracts, preserve exact refusal code and layer, accept no caller digest, use distinct stable domains, and keep existing full planHash/criteriaDigest behavior byte-for-byte unchanged.

Focused tests assert positive roster counts, mutate every included and excluded authoritative field against the production functions, pin exact upstream code/layer refusals, and mutation-drill each digest projector so named assertions go red.

`pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exits 0 and prints nonzero Test Files and Tests counts; the two modified production sources remain <=250 physical lines and the task records the NodeAuthority consumer id before completion.
taskRails: Do not reinterpret PlanRevision.graphBinding or AcceptanceContract.applicability as a proposal-base binding; the new identities are explicitly graph-independent companion digests, while existing full digests remain authoritative for outer approval.
Do not include revision IDs indirectly in node authority through these digests; design line 255 explicitly excludes revision IDs and mutable status.
Touch only the two existing codec sources plus one focused test; root publication remains task-dc21cb4a8f2a4c1c902f3bf3a82a59c2.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — NEW packages/core/src/planning/planning-content-identity.test.ts (the rail's single focused test; pure functions, no store). Against the two not-yet-existing derivations: (a) PLAN EXECUTION-CONTENT DIGEST: admitted PlanRevision → frozen {ok:true, digest} that is STABLE across re-derivation; INCLUDED-FIELD SENSITIVITY — mutating each included field (a step's kind/description/stepId, step ORDER, affectedNodeIds/affectedCriterionIds membership, verificationRecipeRefs) through the PRODUCTION admit-then-derive path changes the digest (one assertion per field, positive generated count over the field table); EXCLUSION PROOF — mutating each excluded field (graphContentHash, graphRevisionRef, approvalState, authorRef, parentRevisionId, rejectionRef, revisionId) leaves the digest BYTE-IDENTICAL (this is the cycle-break DoD 1 demands — assert equality, not just success); (b) CRITERION CONTENT ROSTER: admitted AcceptanceContract → sorted frozen NONEMPTY roster of {criterionId, contentDigest}; per-criterion sensitivity (statement/evidenceRequirements/verificationRecipeRefs/nodeKind/version change that criterion's digest); ISOLATION — changing criterion A's content leaves criterion B's digest byte-identical, and excluded fields (applicability graph/revision/nodeIds, authorRef, contractId) change NO digest; roster sorted by criterionId and its count equals the contract's criteria count (positive, asserted); (c) ADMISSION FIRST: a malformed record refuses with the EXISTING codec's exact upstream code AND layer preserved — the derivations never accept a caller digest and never re-validate independently; (d) DOMAIN SEPARATION: the two derivations use distinct versioned domain strings, and neither equals the existing planHash/criteriaDigest domain — prove by asserting the same logical content yields three pairwise-distinct digests (full vs execution-content vs a criterion digest); (e) BYTE-COMPAT GUARD: existing encode/admit paths' planHash and criteriaDigest outputs on a fixed fixture are byte-identical before and after this task (pin the two hex values from the CURRENT production output in the red run — anti-tautology: derive them from production at baseline, not by hand).
